articleTitle: A Study of Vibration Signal Feature Extraction for Bone Drilling Layer Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Mechanical Engineering and Robotics Research (ICMERR)
abstract: In modern orthopedic surgery, bone drilling is an essential and popular technique used for various purposes such as fracture fixation, bone grafting, joint arthroplasty, and others. This study focuses on measuring and analyzing drilling vibration in orthopedic surgery during bone drilling to address common issues that may arise. The vibration signal of the drill is measured using accelerometer sensors placed near the drill and on the bone in order to avoid any unnecessary vibration signal attenuation. This research specifically examines bone drilling on a cow femur as its bone composition is similar to that of humans. 50,000 vibration signal data are obtained and will be researched to feature extraction for the purpose of classifying layers in bones. The feature extraction method (also called characteristics and signatures) that will be used in this study is presented and grouped into two categories: time-domain features extraction and frequency-domain features extraction. The data collected on the x-, y-, and z-axis of ten drilled holes are used to get feature extraction which is grouped into three classes: layer 1 (periosteum), layer 2 (first cortical), and layer 3 (spongy). The study identifies six feature combinations that have feature values that do not overlap with each other. In the time-domain feature extraction, Mean, RMS, Skewness, and Kurtosis are extracted, while in the frequency-domain feature extraction, root mean square frequency (RMSF), and root variance frequency (RVF) produce good classification results compared to other features.

articleTitle: Control of Variable-Size Wheeled Mobile Robots
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Mechanical Engineering and Robotics Research (ICMERR)
abstract: Due to the shortcomings of the non-deformable rim structure, traditional wheeled mobile robots are difficult to apply in small, complex or rugged and dangerous environments. With the deepening of origami research in the field of engineering, the method of designing mechanisms using the deformable principle has attracted the attention of scholars. Based on the current research on mobile robots, this paper proposes a variable-diameter wheeled robot based on the structure of water bombs. According to the structural characteristics and functional requirements of the robot, the paper completes the selection of relevant hardware. In addition, this paper uses MATLAB to analyze the spatial attitude change of the wheel body driven by the motor, and after in-depth understanding of the control principle of each component, the control system suitable for the mechanical structure is built by integrating the contents of wheel drive, wheel deformation, body steering, environmental perception, and upper computer control. At the end of this paper, the experiment verifies the correctness of the control scheme and shows the application value of variable diameter robot in specific application environment.

articleTitle: Simulation of Integrated Identification of Aerodynamic Parameters and Thrust of Cruise Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Mechanical Engineering and Robotics Research (ICMERR)
abstract: Considering the characteristics of thrust and aerodynamic coupling of the cruise vehicle, this paper proposed a method for integrated online identification and prediction of aerodynamic parameters and thrust of the supersonic cruise vehicle. The research object of this paper is supersonic cruise vehicle powered by solid rocket ramjet. The thrust model of solid rocket ramjet is established based on the thrust characteristic analysis, and the aerodynamic parameter model is established based on the modified wind tunnel test data. Then utilizing the real-time measurement data from the airborne sensor, the parameters of thrust and aerodynamics can be obtained online. The simulation results show that this method has high identification and prediction accuracy, and could provide a feasible solution for online identification and prediction of the performance parameters of the supersonic cruise vehicle.

articleTitle: Optimum Design of Bottom Stirring Impeller for Cosmetics Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Mechanical Engineering and Robotics Research (ICMERR)
abstract: Stirring is an essential process in the production of cosmetics. During this process, the viscosity improver is stirred with a chemical liquid to prevent dripping and evaporation. Bottom stirring vessels are also used in the stirring process because they are suitable for multipurpose stirring and are easy to clean after stirring. However, in practical use, uniform stirring is challenging to achieve since the vessel creates many agglomerates. In this study, we clarified the characteristics of these agglomerates and the flow phenomena around the impeller to crush agglomerates better. We also developed a new impeller with bottom stirring to avoid agglomeration, and it is suitable for many items and small-batch manufacturing. Its effectiveness was verified by conducting experiments comparing our newly developed impeller with other impellers.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a New Bionic Airship with Combined Floatation
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Mechanical Engineering and Robotics Research (ICMERR)
abstract: Traditional airships realize their own control by EFCS (Electronic Flight Control System) driving the front and rear auxiliary airbags, pitching moment of hull and rudder surface during forward flight. In order to meet the requirement of heavy load, the shape dimension is also very large, which easily causes the tension of the skin material to exceed the allowable limit of the material, and will cause greater resistance during flight, which limits its use. In order to reduce drag and improve lift force, a new combined floating-lift integrated biomimetic airship is studied in this paper. This kind of airship is a floating-lift hybrid airship which is slightly heavier than air by properly combining traditional static-buoyant airship with other lift-source airships. It combines the advantages of traditional static-buoyant airship with other dynamic-lift airships and has high lift-drag ratio, heavy load, high controllability, high flight speed and so on. The ground control system has the advantage of simplicity, which can better exert the common advantages of buoyant and dynamic lifting body, so as to improve the aerodynamic performance and loading capacity of airship.

articleTitle: Failure Analysis for the Vertical Shaft of the Lifting Sling
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Mechanical Engineering and Robotics Research (ICMERR)
abstract: Combining with a certain case of vertical shaft failure of Type QD13 overhead crane, this paper gives a detailed discussion, analysis and problem location from many aspects including strength design, metallographic structure of materials, and machining process, etc. Through the comprehensive analysis method integrating the auxiliary tests, experimental study, and theoretical analysis, this paper deduces the critical factor leading to vertical shaft failure. As a result, this paper provides experience for the design and manufacture of related lifting sling, so as to avoid similar problems.

articleTitle: Stability of a Decelerated Flow in a Plane Channel
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Mechanical Engineering and Robotics Research (ICMERR)
abstract: Linear stability of a rapidly decelerated channel flow is considered in the present paper. The base flow velocity distribution is found analytically using the method of the Laplace transform. Deceleration occurs due to a sudden reduction of the flow rate. Linear stability of the base flow is investigated numerically using the collocation method based on Chebyshev polynomials. Linear stability calculations show stabilization of the flow as the ratio of the flow rate after the transient to the flow rate before the transient increases.

articleTitle: Classification of Human Postures
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Mechanical Engineering and Robotics Research (ICMERR)
abstract: The classification of human postures is required in various aspects such as the description of human activities, the synthesis of humanoid robots’ movement, and in the research on robots cooperating with humans. The presented research aims to develop the method for posture classification using the data recorded by the RGB-D cameras. The method enables the recognition of the activity represented by the sequence of human postures viewed in the sagittal plane. The competitive neural network (cNN) was used. The method enables the fast recognition of human activity and is useful for ‘learning by observation’ robots.

articleTitle: Overview of Synthetic Data Generation for Computer Vision in Industry
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Mechanical Engineering and Robotics Research (ICMERR)
abstract: The introduction of Industrial Artificial Intelligence led us to adopt a variety of innovative technologies that add value to the product’s life cycle. One such breakthrough is computer vision-based quality inspection of manufactured products. The main challenge with implementing computer vision in industry is that of a shortage of dataset for training the neural networks. The main objective of this study is to provide an overview of the various methods available for synthetic data generation that can be utilized by industries. We emphasize on flexible production systems that produce unique products every time. The performance of an Object Detection model trained on real and synthetic datasets is used to validate one of the approaches.

articleTitle: Descent Vehicle Movement Control by the Angular Position Change Method Payload
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Mechanical Engineering and Robotics Research (ICMERR)
abstract: An analysis of the rotational motion resulting from the control of the descent vehicle is presented in the paper. The descent vehicle is controlled by the method of shifting the center of mass, which occurs due to a change in the angular position of the payload. The analysis of rotational motion consists in revealing the peculiarities in the motion of the descent vehicle controlled by the above method. To carry out this analysis, a mathematical model of the rotational motion of the descent vehicle has been compiled in this work. Modeling of the angular motion was performed using the developed software that implements the 4th order Runge-Kutta method. The simulation results are presented in the form of graphic dependencies, which include the trajectory of a point on the surface of the descent vehicle, as well as the hodograph of the angular velocity vector in a moving coordinate system. Based on the results of the research, conclusions were drawn about the features of the rotational movement during control, as well as the possibility of using this control method.

articleTitle: Development of an Innovative Air-Ground Carrier Platform for Multi-mode Drones
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Mechanical Engineering and Robotics Research (ICMERR)
abstract: The air-ground drone, capable of both ground movement and aerial flight, exhibits enhanced flexibility and adaptability to different environments. In comparison to existing technological solutions, this paper proposes an air-ground drone capable of automatic switching between automotive and flying modes. The drone employs a screw-rod linkage mechanism to drive the retractable and extendable motion of four rotor arms. Through meticulous torque and speed calculations, only a small-sized reduction motor is needed to simultaneously drive the automatic retraction and extension of all four arms. This paper outlines the overall structure and operational principles of the air-ground drone, providing a detailed exploration of the design and core component selection for the screw-rod linkage mechanism. The presented solution serves as a design approach for similar amphibious drone configurations.

articleTitle: PneuBot - A Soft Robotic Link
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Mechanical Engineering and Robotics Research (ICMERR)
abstract: With the advancement in technology, robots are being introduced in most of the production processes to improve the production efficiency. Due to the increasing adoption of robots in industries, the concept of human-robot collaboration has seen an uprising trend where humans and robots work together in a shared workspace such as Industry 5.0 raising concerns about human safety. Collaborative robots known as Cobots are used in industries for this purpose where the robots and the humans work side to side. A higher scale of research has been carried out in the field of optimizing the cobots to provide a safer environment for humans which mainly focuses on accident prevention. Even though the cobots provide a safer environment, the possibility of a robot colliding with humans is still present based on different cobots techniques. This collision would have a lesser importance if the humans feels it as a normal touch. Thus the main idea which is mainly focussed on, in this paper, is to replace the rigid robot links with a soft robot link as the impact during collision is under the tolerable limit for humans. A self-developed soft robot link which uses air as the media for structural support was used. Therefore, a detailed description of the concept of PneuBot and a comparative study on the impact caused by the existing cobots with rigid links along with the force impact of the self-developed robot soft link will be discussed in this paper. A universal robot 5e will be used as a power and force limiting cobot.

articleTitle: Prototype of an intelligent textile based robot skin to expand potential applications for cobot’s
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Mechanical Engineering and Robotics Research (ICMERR)
abstract: Human Robot Collaboration (HRC) already dates couple of decades back. However, as Industry 4.0 and 5.0 demands smart human-centered production technologies, more concerns has been raised in the recent years regarding optimization and adaption of collaborative robots (Cobots). The core idea of HRC focuses on sharing the same workspace and performing a joint task, by both robot and humans. This paper focuses mainly on the development of a textile-based cover for industrial robots, integrated by several sensor arrays, resulting in enabling the sense of the human in the vicinity of the robot. This information is further utilized to manipulate the standard robot control algorithm to facilitate a safe collaboration by adaptive speed control based on the distance of human and robot. Additionally, the cover material is based on textile, which in terms of passive safety, facilitates cushioning effect when collision is occurred. In terms of active safety, it provides a wide area of sensing with several proximity sensors integrated over the skin.

articleTitle: Advancements and Innovations in U-Net for Enhanced Medical Image Segmentation: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Mechanical Engineering and Robotics Research (ICMERR)
abstract: As one of the most prominent network architectures in recent years within the field of medical image segmentation, U-Net has gained widespread adoption due to its exceptional performance, with various extensions continually emerging. Recently, the rapid progress of U-Net has led to a flood of new methods and uses every year. In this context, it becomes imperative to undertake reviews and encapsulate the latest advancements. Such efforts are vital for offering an updated and comprehensible standpoint to researchers interested in this field. This paper highlights the most recent variants of the U-Net, reviews their principles, and summarizes their successful applications by their optimization approaches in medical segmentation tasks. Furthermore, with the success of Transformers in the field of computer vision, there have been many enthusiastic efforts in recent years to apply self-attention mechanisms to medical image segmentation. This paper delves extensively into how the Transformer model empowers the evolution of the U-Net framework in the context of medical image segmentation. Moreover, it also investigates specific use cases of U-Net in micro and macro tasks such as nucleus segmentation, lung and its nodule, liver segmentation, and gastric detection, all of which hold profound significance in clinical diagnostics. Based on comprehensive literature investigation and analysis, this study provides a forward-looking perspective on the future advancement and possible challenges that U-Net could confront.

articleTitle: Exploring the Potential of a Vertical Takeoff and Landing Flying Car
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Mechanical Engineering and Robotics Research (ICMERR)
abstract: The characteristic of vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) aircraft is that it combines the functions of a helicopter and a fixed-wing aircraft. As an important branch of the VTOL aircraft, flying cars have attracted more attention from capital and media. However, most products claiming to be “flying cars” are more like aircraft than cars because they do not have the ability to travel on the ground. Therefore, this paper proposes a new concept of flying car. It ingeniously retracts the wings and multi-rotors through a rotating folding method to achieve a mode conversion from aircraft to vehicle. This paper introduces the concept source, basic dimensions, key components, and preliminary calculation of the flying car. The paper also derives the relationship curve between the propeller size and power device and finally calculates the flying envelope of the flying car. The concept proposed in this paper has the capability of vertical takeoff and landing, long endurance, and ground driving. The conceptual design method proposed in this article can provide design references for similar types of aircraft.

articleTitle: Training a neural network to observe the assembly mode of parallel robots
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Mechanical Engineering and Robotics Research (ICMERR)
abstract: Parallel robots have different solutions to their forward kinematic problem, i.e., their gripper can adopt different possible positions that are compatible with the displacements of the actuated joints. It is necessary to know the position of the gripper to control parallel robots in the operational space. However, usually, only these joint displacements are measured, which results in the indetermination of which of these possible positions is the one actually adopted by the gripper. Previous methods require redundant sensors to measure directly the position of the gripper or the displacements of passive joints. In this paper we propose to estimate the position of the gripper by solving the observability problem of parallel robots regarded as nonlinear dynamical systems. By taking the position coordinates of the gripper as states of the system, it is possible to reconstruct these states from the signals of inputs (control forces) and outputs (displacements of actuated joints) of the system. To that end, we propose a feedforward neural network to perform as the state observer, and we train it using thousands of trajectories. The proposed neural observer is tested on a simulated 2RPR parallel robot, and it is found that, combined with a refinement post-processing based on Newton-Raphson’s iterative method to solve the forward kinematics, the proposed method is able to exactly reconstruct the position of the gripper if the robot starts to move far from Type 2 singularities, at which different solutions merge.
